### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via ISharingService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx`  _(via ISharingService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`  _(via ISharingService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via explainAccessForCaller (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin), installAttachmentAccessHooks (symbol, a top-level function), installCommentAccessHooks (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39e93b9ef936c9cad11642520d45c2ca2755bdf4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9b3cf8256869fbaf416d2323d5c0335d5f06d186` — the merge of head `d35ec05d557a6d9f0ac74ed9a1f691f7dca85865` into base `39e93b9ef936c9cad11642520d45c2ca2755bdf4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9b3cf8256869fbaf416d2323d5c0335d5f06d186 && git checkout 9b3cf8256869fbaf416d2323d5c0335d5f06d186
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 39e93b9ef936c9cad11642520d45c2ca2755bdf4 d35ec05d557a6d9f0ac74ed9a1f691f7dca85865 && git checkout -B drift-repro 39e93b9ef936c9cad11642520d45c2ca2755bdf4 && git merge --no-ff d35ec05d557a6d9f0ac74ed9a1f691f7dca85865

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39e93b9ef936c9cad11642520d45c2ca2755bdf4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 39e93b9ef936c9cad11642520d45c2ca2755bdf4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d35ec05d557a6d9f0ac74ed9a1f691f7dca85865`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts + packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx, .changeset/24646-parent-gates-one-question.md, .changeset/24646-explain-on-behalf-of-write-verdict.md (read against the unchanged enforcement path at this head: packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts write middleware, security-plugin.ts steps 2.6 and 2.7, resolveOperationPrincipals, and packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts). Remainder, the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT as a standalone PR of those files: attachment-access-hooks.test.ts, comment-parent-update-parity.test.ts, explain-enforce-parity.test.ts.

### ① Derived judgments

Net diff read at merge-base `9b2953d62c` (origin/main) against the head; 11 files, +987/−349, the PR's file list and the net diff agree. Each accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, judged:

1. **`sys_attachment` parent gate, `mayEditAttachmentParent` (attachment-access-hooks.ts).** Where the security service serves `explain`, the record-sharing `checkEdit` step (asked with no depth, so at `own`) and the ADR-0055 master-detail step are no longer asked; the parent's record-grained by-id `update` verdict decides alone, admitting only `allowed === true` and `record.visible === true`, and a decision carrying no record verdict refuses. With no sharing service the caller-scoped parent read is still asked first. Widening: a caller whose write depth on the parent object is `unit`, `unit_and_below` or `org`, or one an app-authored row-level update policy admits, now attaches wherever the parent's by-id update admits. RIGHT — ruling item 1 to the letter. All four limbs (attach, parent-editor update and delete, re-point) and `FileAttachmentService.assertMayAttach` (file-attachment-service.ts L246) reach the one exported function (L532), so no limb drifts; a rejection propagates unchanged; refusal codes `ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS` / `ATTACHMENT_DELETE_DENIED` 403 unchanged; uploaders keep their own rows.
2. **`sys_comment` moderation gate, `canEditParent` (comment-access-hooks.ts).** Same composition, same widening, `RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` 403 kept, the not-visible refusal and the posting read rule unchanged, authors keep their own comments. RIGHT — the two gates answer one question the same way, as the card requires.
3. **Degraded kernels (a security service serving no `explain`, or none).** Both gates keep the composition they had: tri-state `checkEdit` at `own` (`allow` admits, `deny` refuses, `abstain` asks `checkControlledByParentWrite`, whose `allow` / `not_applicable` admit, absent member admits the abstention), no sharing service → degraded read alone. RIGHT — a restriction the ruling does not forbid; dropping the steps where no judgement exists would admit every caller, the fail-open the card refuses. No public shape moves: `AttachmentSecurityLike`, `CommentSecurityLike`, `AttachmentSharingLike`, `CommentSharingLike` keep their `Pick` shapes (doc text only); `mayEditAttachmentParent`'s exported signature is unchanged; `parentUpdateAdmits` is module-private in both gates.
4. **`security.explain`'s on-behalf-of record verdict for `update` / `delete` (security-plugin.ts explain binding; explain-engine.ts `applyRecordAttribution`).** `canEditRecord` / `canDeleteRecord` go through `delegatedWriteGate`: as the agent with `__writeScope` = `intersectDelegatedScope(declared, delegatorScope).agentLegScope` and `__delegatorWriteScope` = the delegator's effective write depth, then, only if that admits, as the delegator (`userId` the delegator's, `onBehalfOf` cleared, `__writeScope` = delegator depth); `probeAuthoredRowWrite` is handed the agent leg; a delegation link naming no user refuses. The record verdict ANDs `computeRlsFilter(delegatorSets, object, rlsOp, delegatorContext)` (no floor option) beside the principal's Layer 1 as `recordLayer1`, a fault reported fail-closed on `rls`. Compared with the enforcement path at this head: the sharing write middleware (sharing-plugin.ts L1328–1343) builds its second gate context as `{...exec, userId: onBehalfOf.userId, onBehalfOf: undefined, __writeScope: exec.__delegatorWriteScope}` and hands the authored-row probe `exec` itself; step 2.6 (security-plugin.ts ~L2906–2932) stamps the two depths with the same two evaluator calls; step 2.7 (~L3064–3066) composes the delegator filter with the same call and no options and ANDs it into the same pre-image re-read; `resolveOperationPrincipals` resolves both principals' sets through the same `resolveDelegatorContext` and `resolvePermissionSetsForContext`, refusing a missing delegator. RIGHT — same construction, same order, both directions of the measured fork closed (a row explain refused that the write admits; a row explain admitted that the write refuses). The ordinary caller keeps the pre-existing `withWriteScope`; the delegated READ verdict is untouched and the binding says so. `ExplainDecision` shape unchanged; the `rls` layer's `detail` gains a sentence (reporting text, no contract field).
5. **`ISharingService` prose, the hit (sharing-service.ts L220–258 and the `canEdit` block L306–311).** The "Write DEPTH is an input the CALLER supplies — absent means `own` (#7144)" paragraph now records that the parent-record gates no longer ask this service, that the 2026-08-10 ruling on #7144 is superseded for them by the ruling on #24646 (letter B), what they ask instead and under what admission rule, keeps the `resolveWriteScope` fail-open as the reason the gates never resolve a depth themselves, states why the by-id judgement does not meet it (object-level grant first), and names the one residual path (a kernel serving no `explain`, `checkEdit` at `own`, the narrow direction). The `canEdit` sentence that pointed at the old shape is rewritten to match. No type, member or export moves; the heading the two module headers cite by name is kept, so their pointers still resolve. RIGHT — ruling item 2 verbatim; both gate module headers and their `callerContext` notes state the same rule; no contradictory prose remains in `packages/spec` (security-service.ts's `checkControlledByParentWrite` doc, "such as a gate on a record's attachments or comments", stays true on the no-explain path). `Spec property liveness` success; the prose feeds no generated artifact.
6. **content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx.** The "Create — parent-edit access" section now states the one question, what the verdict composes, the widening in words, and the degraded-kernel paragraph. RIGHT — matches the code read above. Residual nit, no defect: content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx row 9b still names the two gates as the master check's consumers, which stays true where no `explain` is served.
7. **Public surface overall.** No export added, removed or re-typed in service-storage, plugin-audit, plugin-security or spec; `check:generated` is reported unaffected and `Type Check · source gates` is success on the head.

Gate verdicts on `d35ec05d55`, latest run per check name, as read 2026-10-20T04:14Z: success — Auto Label, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped (query-options erasure; slot lookup & corpus; tooling self-tests), No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, filter (27). Skipped by their own predicates — Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Temporal Conformance (5). Still in progress at that read — Test Core 1/6 through 6/6 and Type Check · workspace (7); the queue's green-check condition reads them when they land, this record does not pre-empt them. No failure on the head.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/24646-parent-gates-one-question.md`: `@objectstack/service-storage` minor, `@objectstack/plugin-audit` minor, `@objectstack/spec` minor; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; ruling item 5's sentence verbatim; names what widens, what does not move, the degraded-kernel retention and the spec prose. RIGHT — a widened runtime accept set in two released packages is a feature, and `yes` takes at least `minor` (AGENTS.md post-task step 3); the spec's published contract prose moves with the same ruling, whose item 4 fixes the level at `minor`. `(widening)` is one arm of the closed pair, well-formed.
- `.changeset/24646-explain-on-behalf-of-write-verdict.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-security` patch. RIGHT — a fix in a released package (explain's delegated write verdict diverged from the write it explains) takes a patch, never none; no author-writable key, export or config moves, so nothing breaking and no ADR-0087 marker owed.
- Clause-②: the PR body carries `Clause-②: yes` at the start of a line; the primary changeset carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; the claim (6282082958), the card's protocol-change section and ruling item 4 say the same. Consistent. The review's face is a governed path (`packages/spec/src/contracts/**`), so the served tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, not the declaration face. `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are success on the head.
- `skip-changeset`: not used, not applicable.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6283091147 — deviations, each answered:
1. attachments-access.mdx edited outside the claim's file surface — right: `content/docs/permissions/` is not release-owned, the section would have read false after the change, and `Flag docs affected by code changes` is success.
2. A second changeset beside the named one — right (② above); the fork arm changed published plugin-security behaviour and a fix never ships without a changeset.
3. Explain's delete verdict composed with update — accepted as one change, not escalated: in the write middleware the per-record gate (`canDelete`, ADR-0111 D3) and the step-2.7 filter are the same path for both verbs, so composing `update` alone would have left explain's delete verdict forked from the DELETE it explains; the change stays inside the fork arm's declared surface (the explain binding and engine), is named in the patch changeset, and is pinned by rig 4's delete rows. The parent gates ask only `update`. It exceeds ruling item 3's literal word `update`, in the direction the ruling's stated aim (explain equals the write) requires.
4. One merge of origin/main (79c3d98b98) — procedural; the net diff against merge-base `9b2953d62c` is the 11 files; #24647's landing `71a8b5eed6` is an ancestor of that merge-base, so the `Blocked-by:` was cleared on the tree reviewed.
5. Commit trailer form — right: all five commits carry AGENTS.md's model-free pair (`Claude-Session:` URL and `Co-authored-by: Claude`), the repo rule the pre-push hook enforces; the harness reminder's model-bearing form is the one it refuses.

open_questions[1] degraded kernels — answered, option A (implemented) is right, not escalated: the ruling binds the gates where a by-id update is judged; where no judgement is served there is nothing to defer to, B would admit every caller on such a kernel (fail-open, the opposite of the card's restrictive divergence), and C trades a guarantee for third-party `ISecurityService` implementations for one read. A keeps a documented, pinned (degraded-kernel suites in both gate tests; ablations G3 and C3) restrictive path and changes no behaviour the ruling did not order.

Ruling item 3 — honoured in order: measured first on a real stack in both postures (52 cells, 4 forks, all on-behalf-of callers, both directions), the explain path fixed (7da68682b1), re-measured at 52/52, then the two steps dropped (ba6fb4912c). Neither forbidden arm taken: the steps were not dropped over a fork, and A was not fallen back to.

Ruling item 2's pointer on #7144 — not in the diff; the PR names it as the seat's write after landing. Owed by the seat, not a defect of this head.

Ruling item 4's declaration to the spec seat — `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts` is declared cross-lane in the claim (6282082958), as required.

Pre-registered pin from #24647 — flipped as pre-registered (title and assertion now "the parent gates' one question, the by-id update verdict, admits the row the by-id update admits"), kept load-bearing on the real plugin-audit gate; the refusing row still refuses `RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` / 403.

Not measured (delegated READ verdict) — recorded; ruling B asks only the update verdict, and the binding states the limit in place.

Security-class out-of-scope finding (the write door's own on-behalf-of composition under an app-authored row policy) — outside this card; this PR neither changes nor widens that answer, explain now matches the door there so the gates do too, and the dev reports it to the seat with the reproduction kept off public surfaces. This record states no more than that.
